options: Hiding a class's internal data and exposing controlled access through public methods
Combining multiple classes into a single file
Converting an interface into a class
Running two classes in the same transaction
questions.explain: Encapsulation keeps a class's internal state private and exposes only the behavior you intend, through public methods that control how that state can be read or changed.

questions.q: How many other classes can a single Apex class extend?
options: As many as needed, separated by commas
Zero -- extends is not supported in Apex
Two: one for data, one for behavior
Exactly one -- a class can only extend one existing class
questions.explain: A class can only extend one other class, but it can implement more than one interface -- this is why Apex doesn't support multiple inheritance of classes.

questions.q: What modifier must a parent class's method have before a subclass can override it?
options: static
virtual
private
transient
questions.explain: You can't override a method with the override keyword unless the class (and that method) has been defined as virtual.

questions.q: In the Marker/YellowMarker example, why does calling write() on a variable declared as type Marker but holding a YellowMarker object print the YellowMarker version of the message?
options: Because Apex ignores declared types at runtime entirely
Because YellowMarker's write() method is static
This is polymorphism: the overridden method's behavior depends on the actual object the variable references, not its declared type
It doesn't -- it always prints the Marker version
questions.explain: This is polymorphism: the behavior of write() differs based on the actual object you're calling it on, even though the variable's declared type is the parent class Marker.

questions.q: If RedMarker extends Marker and adds a new method computePrice() that Marker doesn't have, how must a variable be typed to call computePrice()?
options: It must be typed as RedMarker (the extending class), not as Marker
It can be typed as Marker since RedMarker is a Marker
It must be typed as Object
computePrice() can be called without any variable at all
questions.explain: To call the extra methods that only exist on the extending class, the object's type must be the extending class -- Marker-typed variables only see what Marker itself defines.
